title: Botanical & Natural History
description: The art of scientific observation — birds, plants, and the natural world in fine detail.

items.title: John James Audubon discovering his drawings eaten by a rat
items.description_narrative: This color woodblock print dramatically depicts John James Audubon discovering his meticulously rendered natural history drawings, intended for his monumental Birds of America series, chewed and destroyed by a rat. The artwork captures a moment of profound artistic setback and personal despair for the famed ornithologist.
items.tags: audubon, rat, drawings, destruction, ornithology, woodblock print, japanese art, historical anecdote

items.title: Harlequin Duck
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving with aquatint and etching on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: This hand-colored engraving by Robert Havell captures the distinctive plumage of the Harlequin Duck, a species known for its striking patterns. Through the intricate techniques of aquatint and etching, Havell creates a detailed and vibrant natural history illustration.
items.tags: harlequin duck, wildlife, bird, natural history, engraving, hand-colored print, scientific illustration, detailed

items.title: Black Backed Gull
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving with aquatint and etching on cream wove paper
items.description_narrative: This artwork depicts a black-backed gull, rendered through a detailed process of hand-colored engraving, aquatint, and etching. The precise layering of these printmaking techniques on cream wove paper allowed for a rich and accurate representation of the bird.
items.tags: ornithology, scientific illustration, natural history, hand-colored print, engraving, aquatint, bird

items.title: Great American Shrike
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving, with aquatint, on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: This hand-colored engraving by Robert Havell meticulously captures the Great American Shrike, showcasing the bird's distinctive features. The intricate details are rendered through a combination of engraving and aquatint on ivory wove paper, characteristic of natural history illustrations of its time.
items.tags: bird, shrike, engraving, hand-colored, natural history, wildlife, 19th century

items.title: Male Bay Breasted Warbler
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving, with aquatint, on cream wove paper
items.description_narrative: This hand-colored engraving by Robert Havell meticulously depicts a Male Bay Breasted Warbler, showcasing the species with intricate detail. Created in 1829, the artwork represents a tradition of scientific illustration combined with artistic precision.
items.tags: bird, warbler, wildlife, natural history, scientific illustration, engraving, detailed, hand-colored

items.title: Florida Jay
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving, with aquatint, on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: This hand-colored engraving by Robert Havell depicts a vibrant Florida Jay, showcasing intricate details through the aquatint technique. Created in 1830, this work is a testament to the detailed ornithological illustrations of the era.
items.tags: bird, jay, florida, engraving, aquatint, natural history, scientific illustration, ornithology

items.title: Cervus Virginianus
items.description_narrative: This hand-colored lithograph precisely depicts the Cervus Virginianus, commonly known as the White-tailed Deer. Created by John Woodhouse Audubon, the print showcases a detailed rendering of this prominent North American species.
items.tags: animal, wildlife, deer, lithograph, hand-colored, natural history, scientific illustration

items.title: Saint James the Greater
items.medium: Etching in black on cream laid paper
items.description_narrative: This etching depicts Saint James the Greater, rendered in black ink on cream laid paper. The print by Master F. P. utilizes the meticulous detail possible with the etching technique.
items.tags: saint james, religious, etching, print, figure, christian art

items.title: Bust of a Youth (Saint John the Baptist)
items.medium: Marble on variegated black marble socle
items.description_narrative: This marble sculpture by Francesco Mochi depicts a youthful figure, believed to be Saint John the Baptist. Created between 1630 and 1640, it showcases the artist's mastery of the medium.
items.tags: sculpture, marble, baroque, religious, figure, youth, italian

items.title: Martyrdom of Saint Cipriano from Heiligenleben (Lives of the Saints), Plate 18 from Woodcuts from Books of the 15th Century
items.medium: Woodcut in black, and letterpress in black (recto and verso), on cream laid paper
items.description_narrative: This woodcut depicts the Martyrdom of Saint Cipriano, a dramatic scene from the 'Heiligenleben' (Lives of the Saints). Created in 1481 by the Master of the Boccaccio Illustrations, it showcases early printmaking techniques with black ink on cream laid paper.
items.tags: woodcut, martyrdom, saint, religious art, 15th century, printmaking, gothic art

items.title: Botanical Specimen
items.description_narrative: This photogenic drawing by William Henry Fox Talbot, dating from around 1835, captures a botanical specimen. It demonstrates an early photographic process that rendered objects directly onto light-sensitive paper.
items.tags: botanical, nature, early photography, photogenic drawing, scientific, experimental, monochrome

items.title: Roses in a Vase
items.medium: Black Conté crayon on ivory laid paper, discolored to tan, edge mounted on tan wove paper
items.description_narrative: This delicate drawing depicts roses in a vase, rendered with precise strokes of black Conté crayon. Created early in his career, it showcases Georges Seurat's meticulous approach to form and light even before his iconic Pointillist paintings.
items.tags: roses, flowers, still life, drawing, crayon, 19th century, french art

items.title: Kichik Beg Wounded during Babur's Attack on Qalat, from a copy of the Baburnama (Book of Babur)
items.medium: Opaque watercolor and gold on paper
items.description_narrative: This vibrant miniature depicts Kichik Beg being wounded amidst Babur's fierce attack on Qalat, capturing a specific moment of historical conflict. It originates from a richly illustrated copy of the Baburnama, an autobiographical account of the first Mughal emperor.
items.tags: mughal, battle, warfare, baburnama, manuscript, historical, royalty, miniature painting

items.title: Chasuble
items.medium: Silk, warp-float faced 7:1 satin weave with supplementary brocading wefts self-patterned by ground weft floats; edged with silk and gilt-metal-strip-wrapped silk, plain weave with supplementary patterning wefts; lined with linen, plain weave
items.description_narrative: This chasuble, a primary outer vestment worn by clergy, is crafted from silk with intricate supplementary brocading wefts. Its elegant design and luxurious material reflect the skilled textile artistry prevalent in the late 18th century.
items.tags: religious, vestment, silk, brocading, textile, 18th century, ecclesiastical

items.title: Skirt Panel for a Woman's Sack Gown
items.medium: Silk, plain weave foundation with supplementary patterning warps and supplementary brocading wefts
items.description_narrative: This intricate Skirt Panel for a Woman's Sack Gown, designed by Anna Maria Garthwaite in 1749, showcases elaborate silk plain weave with supplementary patterning warps and brocading wefts. Its detailed construction highlights the sophisticated textile artistry of the mid-18th century.
items.tags: textile, silk, fashion, 18th century, design, gown, patterned, weaving

items.title: Panel
items.medium: Silk, plain weave with supplementary patterning warps, supplementary facing wefts and brocading wefts, and self-patterned by two-color complementary ground wefts; two fragments pieced
items.description_narrative: This intricately woven silk panel by Courtois showcases sophisticated textile techniques, including plain weave, supplementary patterning, and brocading wefts. Composed of two pieced fragments, it exemplifies the complex patterns achievable in early 18th-century weaving.
